item.title: Places and directions
item.description: Words for asking the way and explaining where a place is.

children.definition: to change direction and go to the left
children.example: Turn left at the bank and walk for two minutes.

children.definition: to continue in the same direction without turning
children.example: Go straight on until you see the metro station.

children.definition: the place where two streets meet
children.example: The pharmacy is on the corner of the street.

children.definition: on the other side of a street or room, facing something
children.example: The café is opposite the cinema.

children.definition: in the space with one thing on each side
children.example: The bank is between the bakery and the post office.
There's a small car park behind the hotel.

children.definition: a place where two roads cross each other
red, yellow and green lights that tell cars when to stop and go
children.example: Cross the road at the traffic lights.

children.definition: from one part of a road or river towards the other end
children.example: Walk along this street for about five hundred metres.
Is the railway station far from here?

children.definition: to not know where you are or how to find the right way
children.example: I got lost in the old city of Bukhara, but a kind man helped me.

children.definition: the door or gate where you go into a building or place
children.example: Meet me at the main entrance of the park.
